messages.author: befc31f30774e5bc
messages.subject: Overdispersion and mle2
parts:
Hi all,
I've got a quandary.
I am examining differences in population-level responses of Mimulus to water and temperature treatments and have succeeded well in building nonparametric models for most of the response variables except for the most informative one - total seed set.

The issue is overdispersion... severe overdispersion (see attached figure). The figure shows the distribution of this parameter for each of the 5 populations.

How can I overcome this using mle2?  I want to use mle2 because I have already built upon it significantly for all the other variables and don't want to rewrite my code.

Thanks,
Iara

--
Dr. Iara Lacher


PhD - UC Davis Ecology
MESM - Bren School for Environmental Science and Management

messages.author: 64211a3c2877d871
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Overdispersion and mle2
parts:
Hi Iara,

Bolker deals with this problem in the supplemental example that accompanies his GLMM TREE paper. He suggests several graphical means and provides code to assess which distribution might best help you deal with overdispersion (e.g., Poisson, Negative Binomial (Gamma Poisson), etc.) and in his example ends up using a Poisson distribution with an observation-level random effect. He uses glmer, not mle2, but the use of the observation-level random effect (i.e., create a variable with a unique number for each of your observations and include this as a random effect), can be done with either. 

Hope this helps,
Sacha
